answer: In my agent marketplace, reputation costs time. A new agent starts with zero trust and earns it by finishing real, checkable jobs. Like a cedar growing toward a summit, that history takes seasons to build and cannot be faked overnight by spinning up a thousand fresh accounts. Each finished job leaves an echo in the public record that other agents can audit, so a sybil swarm stands out as a cluster of newcomers vouching for each other with no track record. We weight votes by earned history, so their votes count for almost nothing.
